'''David Lyndon Emsley''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]] (born 29 November 1964) is a British chemist specialising in [[solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance]] and a professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne)]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Prof. Lyndon Emsley|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lrm/emsley/|access-date=2021-01-07|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> He was awarded the 2012 [[Grand Prix Charles-Leopold Mayer]] of the French [[Académie des Sciences]] and the 2015 [[List of Royal Society of Chemistry medals and awards|Bourke Award]] of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref name=BourkeEmsley>{{cite web|title=Bourke Award 2015 Winner. Professor Lyndon Emsley|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/BourkeAward/2015-Winner.asp| publisher=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]] |access-date=29 October 2015 |date=2015}}</ref>

He was an editorial board member of the journal ''[[Magnetic Resonance in Chemistry]]'' from 2008 to 2010. He is a member of the Editorial Advisory Board of ''[[ChemPhysChem]]''<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Kira |last1=Welter |first2=Lynsey |last2=Geldeard |first3=Kate |last3=Lawrence |first4=Greta |last4=Heydenrych|title=A Bright Year for Physical Chemistry – Editorial Board Renewal |date=30 December 2014|doi= 10.1002/cphc.201402817 |pmid=25557307 |volume=16 |issue=1 |journal=ChemPhysChem |pages=3–5|doi-access=free }}</ref> and ''[[Solid State Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (journal)|Solid State Nuclear Magnetic Resonance]]''. He is an [[associate editor]] of the ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]''.

==Birth and education==
Emsley is the son of professor James Emsley, of the [[University of Southampton]].<ref name=Nature/> The younger Emsley received his [[Master of Science]] in chemistry from the [[Imperial College of Science and Technology]] in 1986 and received his Ph.D. from the [[Université de Lausanne]] in 1991 under the direction of [[Geoffrey Bodenhausen]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Geoffrey Bodenhausen |url=http://www.paris-en-resonance.fr/CvHtml/cvGeoffrey.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160205084512/http://www.paris-en-resonance.fr/CvHtml/cvGeoffrey.php |url-status=dead |archive-date=5 February 2016 |publisher=www.paris-en-resonance.fr |access-date=11 January 2016 }}</ref> working with NMR spectroscopy of solutions. Before beginning his Ph.D., he had worked more than one year in Great Britain at a firm specializing in [[intellectual property]] law.<ref name=Argent2005>{{Cite magazine|title=Medailles d'argent 2005|url=http://www.cnrs.fr/fr/recherche/prix/docs/2005argent_web.pdf|magazine=[[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]]|access-date=29 October 2015|date=9 October 2010|language=fr|pages=20–21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120709072322/http://www.cnrs.fr/fr/recherche/prix/docs/2005argent_web.pdf|archive-date=9 July 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career==
Emsley began his [[postdoctoral research]] at the [[Miller Institute for Basic Research in Science]] ([[University of California]], Berkeley), where he was introduced to solid-state NMR working with [[Alexander Pines]]. In 1993 he moved to the [[Commissariat à l'énergie atomique et aux énergies alternatives|French National Laboratory for Atomic Energy Research]] in [[Grenoble]], where he worked as a post-doc with Claude Roby and Michel Bardet.<ref name=Argent2005/>

In October 1994 he was appointed to a Professorship (''Professeur associé'') at the Ecole normale supérieure in Lyon, and became Full Professor in 1995. In Lyon he was the head of the Experimental Chemistry Laboratory from 1999 to 2002, and director of the Chemistry Department from 2006 to 2014. <!-- In 1999 he was a founding organiser of the bis-annual Alpine Conference on Solid State NMR in [[Chamonix]]. www.alpine-conference.org --> In 2002 he became a member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]].<ref name=IUF>{{cite web |title=Lyndon Emsley |url=http://www.iufrance.fr/les-membres-de-liuf/membre/876-lyndon-emsley.html |publisher=[[Institut Universitaire de France]]|access-date=1 January 2016|language=fr}}</ref>

[[File:Institut des Sciences Analytiques Lyon CEMAGREF August 2012.JPG|thumb|left|The newly completed ISA area in August 2012; the CRMN building is on the left]]

In 2003 Emsley was appointed as project leader for the creation in [[Villeurbanne]] of the ''[[Centre Européen de Résonance Magnétique Nucléaire à Très Hauts Champs]]'' (CRMN, European Laboratory for Very High Field NMR), which was the first step in launching the forthcoming [[Institute of Analytical Sciences]] (ISA). The building of the new laboratory was completed in 2008.<ref name=BourkeEmsley/><!--a joint laboratory (''unité mixte'') of the ENS Lyon, the CNRS and the [[Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1]] -->

Since 2011, he has been an associate editor of the ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=ASSOCIATE EDITORS|url=https://pubs.acs.org/userimages/ContentEditor/1233861031697/jacsat-eab.pdf |access-date=29 October 2015 }}</ref>

In 2012 he was promoted to Senior Member of the ''Institut Universitaire de France''.<ref name=IUF/>

In June 2014 he moved to the EPFL as a professor of physical chemistry,<ref name=nominationEPFL>{{cite journal|title=Nominations of EPFL professors|url=http://actu.epfl.ch/news/nominations-of-epfl-professors-17/ |journal=[[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] |access-date=13 January 2015 |date=25 May 2015|last1=Evangelista|first1=Sandy}}</ref> where he is currently director of the ''Laboratoire de résonance magnétique'' of the ISIC (Institute of chemical sciences and engineering).<ref name=BourkeEmsley/>

In 2015 he received the Bourke award "for the development of experimental methods that have transformed the field of solid-state NMR and enabled new applications across chemistry".<ref name=BourkeEmsley/>

==Research==
Emsley's main research field is solid-state NMR spectroscopy, specifically the development of new spectroscopic methods for the determination the atomic-level structure, the dynamics and the reactivity of a wide range of materials and molecular systems, that have been inaccessible with other analytical methods.<ref name=nominationEPFL/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Blanc |first1=Frédéric|last2=Copéret |first2=Christophe|last3= Lesage|first3=Anne|last4=Lyndon |first4=Emsley  |title=High resolution solid state NMR spectroscopy in surface organometallic chemistry: access to molecular understanding of active sites of well-defined heterogeneous catalysts|doi=10.1039/b612793m |pmid=18224261|journal=Chem. Soc. Rev. |date=2008 |volume=37 |pages=518–526 |quote= Lyndon and Anne have been developing new NMR methods for the study of the structure and dynamics of a wide range of solidstate compounds at the Chemistry Department of the Ecole Normale Supérieure de Lyon (ENS Lyon) |issue=3}}</ref><ref name=Extance2017>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/solid-3d-nmr-evidence-reaches-the-surface/2500289.article|title=Solid 3D NMR evidence reaches the surface|date=23 January 2017|last=Extance|first=Andy |access-date=13 November 2024|magazine=[[Chemistry World]]}}</ref>

He published articles in NMR crystallography,<ref name=Highlights2009>{{cite news |last= Robinson |first= Philip|date= 26 February 2009|title=Crystal clear method for identifying powders |url=http://www.rsc.org/Publishing/ChemTech/Volume/2009/04/identifying_powders.asp |newspaper=Highlights in Chemical Technology |access-date=22 October 2015}}</ref> structural biology, protein dynamics,<ref>{{cite news |date=30 April 2015 |title=Waking proteins up from deep sleep to study their motions |url=http://phys.org/news/2015-04-proteins-deep-motions.html |access-date=22 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=5 January 2015 |title=Forscher schauten Proteinen bei der Arbeit zu |url=http://kurier.at/lebensart/leben/forscher-schauten-proteinen-bei-der-arbeit-zu/128.114.726 |newspaper=[[Kurier]]|language=de|access-date=22 October 2015 }}</ref> [[dynamic nuclear polarization]] (DNP) enhanced
surface NMR spectroscopy<ref name=Extance2017/> and [[Magnetic resonance imaging|MRI]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Loumé |first=Lise |date= 30 September 2014|title=Imagerie médicale : vers un diagnostic à moindre risque ?|url=http://www.sciencesetavenir.fr/sante/20140930.OBS0652/imagerie-medicale-vers-un-diagnostic-a-moindre-risque.html |newspaper=[[Sciences et Avenir]] |access-date=28 October 2015}}</ref><ref name=thz>{{cite web |last= Rüegg |first=Peter |date=30 September 2014|title=Bessere Auflösung dank Hyperpolarisation |url=https://www.ethz.ch/de/news-und-veranstaltungen/eth-news/news/2014/09/MRI-imaging-technology-enhanced-by-hyperpolarization.html |editor=ethz |language=de |access-date=3 January 2016}}</ref>

His work has involved several collaborations with the [[Bruker Corporation]]. In 2010, under his supervision as scientific director, the CRMN acquired and began using the world's most powerful currently operating [[NMR spectrometer]], which breaks the [[Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy#Resonant frequency|billion-hertz]] barrier.<ref name=Nature>{{cite journal |last= Bhattacharya |first=Ananyo |date=2010 |title=Chemistry: Breaking the billion-hertz barrier |journal=Nature |volume=463 |issue=7281 |pages=605–606 |doi=10.1038/463605a |pmid=20130626|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Le spectromètre le plus puissant au monde|url=http://www2.cnrs.fr/presse/communique/1692.htm| publisher=[[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] |access-date=28 October 2015 |date=9 October 2010 |language=fr}}</ref> CRMN was also one of the first laboratories in the world to install a high field (800&nbsp;MHz proton resonant frequency) solid state DNP accessory<ref>{{cite web |last1=Emsley|first1=Lyndon|last2=Lesage|first2=Anne|title=Surface Enhanced NMR Spectroscopy by Dynamic Nuclear Polarisation |url=http://palse.universite-lyon.fr/servlet/com.univ.collaboratif.utils.LectureFichiergw?ID_FICHIER=1251709148177&ID_FICHE=131190|year=2010|access-date=2 January 2016}}</ref> and to test the new very fast 0.7&nbsp;mm MAS rotors.<ref>{{cite web|title=适用于超快速魔角自旋的 111 kHz 探头 NMR 分析为生物固体和材料分析带来全新见解|url=https://www.bruker.com/cn/products/mr/nmr/probes/probes/solids/very-fast-mas/07-mm/overview.html|language=zh|access-date=16 June 2017}}{{Dead link|date=October 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Solid-state NMR sequences===
Emsley worked with colleague [[Anne Lesage]] to introduce new through-bond carbon-proton correlation techniques in [[Solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance#Modern solid-state NMR spectroscopy|CP]]-[[Magic angle spinning|MAS]] NMR, namely the MAS-J-[[Heteronuclear single quantum coherence spectroscopy|HSQC]] and MAS-J-[[HMQC]] experiments, both used to improve resolution of two-dimensional heteronuclear correlation spectra through bond homonuclear correlations with the refocused INADEQUATE experiment in solids. They showed also the feasibility of ssNMR spectral editing techniques making use of heteronuclear scalar couplings.<ref name=Lesage1998>{{cite journal |last1=Lesage |first1=Anne |last2= Steuernagel |first2=Stefan |last3= Emsley |first3=Lyndon |date=1998 |title=Carbon-13 Spectral Editing in Solid-State NMR Using Heteronuclear Scalar Couplings |journal= J. Am. Chem. Soc.|volume=120 |issue= 28|pages= 7095–7100|doi=10.1021/ja981019t |bibcode=1998JAChS.120.7095L |url=https://infoscience.epfl.ch/handle/20.500.14299/110155 }}</ref>

These implementations paved the way to the spectral characterization of solid samples at natural isotopic abundance, in a manner similar to liquid-state NMR.<ref name=Lesage1998/>

It was therefore possible use scalar couplings to probe weak bonding interactions in solids and provide the 
first ever direct detection of a [[hydrogen bond]] in the solid-state,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brown |first1=S. P. |last2=Torralba |first2=M. P. |last3= Sanz |first3= D. |first4=R. M.|last4=Claramunt |first5=Lyndon|last5= Emsley|date=January 2002 |title=The Direct Detection of a Hydrogen Bond in the Solid State by NMR through the Observation of a Hydrogen-Bond Mediated 15N−15N J Coupling |journal=J. Am. Chem. Soc. |volume=124 |issue=7 |pages=1152–1153 |doi=10.1021/ja0172262 |pmid=11841267 |bibcode=2002JAChS.124.1152B |url=https://infoscience.epfl.ch/handle/20.500.14299/110117 }}</ref> as well as the first experimental demonstration of the presence of [[agostic interaction]]s in surface species, indicated by [[Carbene|carbenic]] [[J-coupling|<math>J_{C-H}</math>]].

His team also introduced a theoretical framework for the application of continuously phase modulated radio-frequency pulses for homonuclear decoupling in solid-state NMR, allowing new families of decoupling sequences.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sakellariou |first1=Dimitris |last2=Lesage |first2=Anne |last3=Hodgkinson |first3= Paul |first4=Lyndon|last4= Emsley|date=March 2000 |title=Homonuclear dipolar decoupling in solid-state NMR using continuous phase modulation |journal=Chem. Phys. Lett. |volume=319 |issue=3–4 |pages=253–260 |doi=10.1016/S0009-2614(00)00127-5 |bibcode=2000CPL...319..253S}}</ref> This allowed them to obtain high-resolution proton spectra in solids.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Lesage |first1=Anne |last2= Luminita |first2=Duma |last3=Sakellariou |first3=Dimitris |first4=Lyndon|last4= Emsley |date=2001 |title=Improved Resolution in Proton NMR Spectroscopy of Powdered Solids |journal= J. Am. Chem. Soc.|volume=123 |issue=24 |pages=5747–5752 |doi=10.1021/ja0039740 |pmid=11403608 |bibcode=2001JAChS.123.5747L |url=https://infoscience.epfl.ch/handle/20.500.14299/110124 }}</ref> a key step for three-dimensional structure determination of  organic and inorganic materials at natural isotopic abundance.

===NMR Crystallography===
{{See also|Nuclear magnetic resonance crystallography}}
The improvements in the area of proton ssNMR, specifically homonuclear decoupling, set the field for the development of NMR Crystallography.<ref name=Bradley2005>{{cite magazine |first=David|last= Bradley|date= 15 August 2005|title=Crystallography by NMR |url=http://www.spectroscopynow.com/details/ezine/sepspec11132ezine/Crystallography-by-NMR.html?&tzcheck=1 |magazine=SpectroscopyNOW |access-date=8 January 2016}}</ref>

Contrary to X-ray, single crystals are not necessary with ssNMR and structural information can be obtained from high-resolution spectra of disordered solids.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sakellariou  |first1=Dimitris  |last2= Brown |first2= Steven P.|last3=Lesage |first3=Anne |last4= Hediger |first4=Sabine  |last5= Bardet |first5= Michel |last6= Meriles |first6= Carlos A. |last7=Pines |first7= Alexander |first8=Lyndon |last8= Emsley|date= 2003 |title=High Resolution NMR Correlation Spectra of Disordered Solids |journal=J. Am. Chem. Soc. |volume=125 |issue= 14|pages=4376–4380 |doi=10.1021/ja0292389 |pmid=12670262 |bibcode=2003JAChS.125.4376S |s2cid=8079811 }}</ref>

In 2009 Emsley's group showed the possibility of total structure determination of drug-sized organic molecules through the combination of [[density functional theory]] and solid-state NMR.<ref name=Highlights2009/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Salager |first1=Elodie |last2=Stein |first2=Robin S. |last3= Pickard |first3= Chris J. |first4=Bénédicte|last4= Elena |first5=Lyndon |last5= Emsley|date= April 2009 |title=Powder NMR crystallography of thymol |pmid=19421517 |journal=Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. |volume=11 |issue=15 |pages=2610–21 |doi=10.1039/b821018g |bibcode=2009PCCP...11.2610S}}</ref>

===Surface catalysis===
Emsley and co-workers have shown that multi-dimensional solid state NMR can be exploited to chemically and structurally characterize catalytic surface species at a molecular level, such as reaction intermediates and catalytic centres of [[heterogeneous catalysts]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Blanc  |first1=Frédéric  |last2= Christophe |first2=Copéret |last3= Lesage |first3= Anne |first4=Lyndon |last4= Emsley|date= 2008 |title=High resolution solid state NMR spectroscopy in surface organometallic chemistry: access to molecular understanding of active sites of well-defined heterogeneous catalysts |journal= Chem. Soc. Rev. |volume= 37|issue=3 |pages=518–526 |doi= 10.1039/B612793M |pmid=18224261 }}</ref>

===DNP-enhanced surface NMR spectroscopy===
In the field of surface chemistry, Emsley and co-workers introduced a new approach in the characterization of surfaces through ssNMR, called Surface Enhanced NMR Spectroscopy (SENS). Some systems on various support materials of great chemical interest are below the sensitivity limit of detection for the technique, but such low [[detection limit]] can be boosted using DNP, coupled with isotopic labeling and high magnetic fields. This approach enhances surface NMR signals allowing the analysis of near-surface species or materials with surface areas three orders of magnitude lower than before (around 1 [[square meter|m<sup>2</sup>]]/[[gram|g]], instead of 1000 m<sup>2</sup>/g).<ref name=ERC3449400>{{cite web|title=Surface Enhanced NMR Spectroscopy|url=https://erc.europa.eu/surface-enhanced-nmr-spectroscopy|publisher=[[European Research Council]]|access-date=29 October 2015}}</ref>

Through DNP, transfer of polarization and relevant signal enhancement can occur from the protons of the solvent batch to the rarer nuclei at natural isotopic abundance on the surface framework, including species covalently bonded to the latter one.<ref>{{cite journal|first1= Anne |last1=Lesage |first2= Moreno |last2= Lelli  |first3= David |last3=Gajan  |first4=Marc A. |last4=Caporini |first5= Veronika|last5= Vitzthum|first6= Pascal |last6= Miéville |first7=Johan   |last7=Alauzun |first8= Arthur  |last8= Roussey |first9= Chloé|last9=Thieuleux |first10=Ahmad   |last10=Geoffrey  |first11=Geoffrey |last11=Bodenhausen |first12=Christophe |last12=Coperet|first13= Lyndon |last13=Emsley |title=Surface Enhanced NMR Spectroscopy by Dynamic Nuclear Polarization |date= 2010 |volume=132 |issue=44 |pages=15459–15461 |doi=10.1021/ja104771z |pmid=20831165 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|bibcode=2010JAChS.13215459L |url=https://zenodo.org/record/45688 }}</ref>

Thanks to the description of physicochemically distinct adsorption interactions, new insights can also be offered in hydratation phenomena.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Rahul P.|last1=Sangodkar |first2=Benjamin J.|last2=Smith |first3= David |last3=Gajan  |first4= Aaron J. |last4=Rossini |first5= Lawrence R. |last5=Roberts |first6= Gary P. |last6=Funkhouser  |first7= Anne |last7=Lesage  |first8= Lyndon |last8=Emsley |first9= Bradley F. |last9=Chmelka |title=Influences of Dilute Organic Adsorbates on the Hydration of Low-Surface-Area Silicates |volume=137 |issue=25 |pages=8096–8112 |doi=10.1021/jacs.5b00622 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|year=2015 |pmid=26029958|doi-access=free |bibcode=2015JAChS.137.8096S }}</ref>

===Paramagnetic systems===
Another subject concerns the study of paramagnetic systems, such as  4Fe-4S,<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Crozet |first1=M. |last2= Chaussade |first2= M. |last3= Bardet |first3= M. |last4= Emsley |first4= L. |last5= Lamotte |first5= B. |last6= Mouesca |first6= J. M. |date= 2000 |title=13 C Solid State NMR Studies on Synthetic Model Compounds of [4Fe 4S] Clusters in the 2+ State |journal=J. Phys. Chem. A |volume= 104 |issue=44 |pages= 9990–10000 |doi= 10.1021/jp002005o|bibcode=2000JPCA..104.9990C }}</ref>  high  spin  Fe(II) catalyst,  lanthanide-containing  complexes or paramagnetic centers in proteins, with specific attention to the development of NMR methods specifically  aimed at paramagnetic  solids.

===Solid-state NMR of proteins and bioaggregates===
The CRMN was one of the groups developing tools and protocols for the [[Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy of proteins|structural and dynamic characterization of proteins]] in solid phase, including preparations of micro-crystalline samples, role of solvent,<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Lesage |first1=A. |last2= Gardiennet |first2=C. |last3= Loquet |first3= A. |last4= Verel |first4= R. |last5= Emsley |first5= L. |last6= Meier |first6= B.H.|last7= Böckmann |first7= A.|date= July 2008 |title=Polarization Transfer over the Water Protein Interface in Solid Proteins |journal=Angew. Chem. |volume=47 |issue= 31|pages= 5851–5854 |doi= 10.1002/anie.200801110|pmid=18613186 |doi-access= free }}</ref> paramagnetic systems and [[Triple-resonance nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy|sequential assignment]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Pintacuda |first1=Guido |last2= Giraud |first2=Nicolas |last3= Pierattelli |first3= Roberta |last4= Böckmann |first4= Anja |last5= Bertini |first5= Ivano |last6= Emsley |first6= Lyndon |date= December 2006 |title=Solid State NMR of a Paramagnetic Protein: Assignment and Study of Human Dimeric Oxidized Cu(II),Zn(II) Superoxide Dismutase (SOD) |journal=Angew. Chem. |volume=46 |issue= 7|pages= 1079–1082 |doi= 10.1002/anie.200603093 |pmid=17191298 }}</ref> with a progressive introduction thanks to ultra-fast MAS of direct proton acquisition mimicking the sequences used for liquid NMR spectra.<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Marchetti |first1=Alessandro |last2= Jehle |first2=Stefan |last3= Felletti |first3= Michele |last4= Knight |first4= Michael J. |last5= Wang |first5=Yao |last6=Xu  |first6=Zhi-Qiang  |last7=Park  |first7=Ah Young |last8= Otting |first8=Gottfried |last9= Lesage |first9= Anne |last10= Emsley |first10= Lyndon |last11=Dixon  |first11=Nicholas E. |last12=Pintacuda  |first12= Guido |date= July 2012 |title=Backbone Assignment of Fully Protonated Solid Proteins by 1H Detection and Ultrafast Magic-Angle-Spinning NMR Spectroscopy |journal=Angew. Chem. |volume= 51  |issue=43 |pages=10756–10759 |doi=10.1002/anie.201203124 |pmid=23023570 }}</ref>

In collaboration with [[Martin Blackledge]] his team published some of the first ssNMR methods for the characterization of atom-specific dynamics in biosolids and its relation with solvent behaviour and function, providing detailed insight about the hierarchy of motions in proteins with the increase of temperature.<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Lewandowski |first1=J. |last2= ChHalseaussade |first2= M.E. |last3= Blackledge |first3= M. |last4= Emsley |first4= L.|date= May 2015 |title=Direct observation of hierarchical protein dynamics |pmid=25931561 |journal=Science |volume=348 |issue= 6234 |pages= 578–81 |doi=10.1126/science.aaa6111 |bibcode=2015Sci...348..578L |s2cid=10385759 |url=http://wrap.warwick.ac.uk/71583/1/WRAP_1071602-ch-240815-lewandowski_accepted_manuscript.pdf }}</ref><ref name=Physorg>{{cite news |date= 30 April 2015|title=Waking proteins up from deep sleep to study their motions |url=http://www.rsc.org/Publishing/ChemTech/Volume/2009/04/identifying_powders.asp |newspaper=[[Phys.org]] |access-date=1 January 2016}}</ref>

===Whole organism NMR===
With [[Laurent Ségalat]] Emsley showed on the [[model organism]] ''[[Caenorhabditis elegans]]'' the possibility to use ssNMR on a whole organism for the understanding of its metabolic pattern and the influence of drug assumption or genetic modifications.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Blaise  |first1=Benjamin J. |last2=Giacomotto |first2=Jean |last3= Elena |first3=Bénédicte |first4=Dumas |last4= Marc-Emmanuel |first5=Pierre |last5=Toulhoat |first6=Laurent |last6=Ségalat |first7=Lyndon |last7=Emsley |date=December 2007 |title=Metabotyping of Caenorhabditis elegans reveals latent phenotypes |pmc=2148380 |journal= Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci.|volume=104 |issue=50 |pages=19808–19812 |doi= 10.1073/pnas.0707393104 |pmid=18077412|bibcode=2007PNAS..10419808B |doi-access=free }}</ref>
